best_human.source: Stephen Ainley, Mathematical Puzzles (1977), attributed in OEIS A250000; the layout is transcribed in Kamenetsky's 2019 file.
best_human.provenance: Traditional human construction. It predates modern generative AI; the saved witness is a later public transcription.
best_human.evidence_state: The complete board is reproduced and passes exact pairwise checking.

best_public.source: OEIS A250000, Kamenetsky's best-known-solution file, line headed a(30)>=131.
best_public.provenance: Public construction attributed to Ainley (1977), with a later 2019 layout transcription. No AI authorship claim is made for the historical construction.
best_public.evidence_state: Verified as a feasible lower bound; no n=30 optimum claim.

best_reproduced.verification_method: Recount each army and check every white-black pair for row, column, and diagonal attacks.
best_reproduced.origin_type: historical construction parsed from an OEIS public layout

frozen_human_baseline.endpoint_policy: Freeze the exact integer arm size as H for J/H.

highest_reported.source: OEIS A250000, Kamenetsky, Best known solutions for 12<=n<=30.
highest_reported.reproduction_status: The layout is reproduced. It establishes a lower bound only; optimality at n=30 is open in the sources checked.

optimality_status.evidence: The finite 225 row/column bound follows from disjoint occupied rows and columns for opposite colors. The 2025 asymptotic upper bound is stated only for sufficiently large n and is not applied to n=30. A separate INFORMS paper establishes n=16=37, not n=30.
